text:
Alex Chen: Heads up — I noticed a ~30% throughput regression on mixtral-8x7b after we enabled RoPE scaling + paged KV. Profiler shows kernel fallback to generic matmul in the attention path. Saving raw traces now.

Priya Rao: Can you paste the runtime config? Is this GQA or MQA?

Alex Chen: GQA. Quick config excerpt: 
```
model: mixtral-8x7b
kv_layout: paged
num_key_value_heads: 64
kv_dim: 128
rope_scale: 1.8
paged_kv_page_size: 128
```
Seeing a lot of small GPU kernels instead of the fused attention/kv kernel.

perf-bot: nightly-bench/mixtral-8x7b GQA (paged) baseline -> throughput=480 tok/s, p50=120ms, p95=430ms; after change -> throughput=340 tok/s, p50=170ms, GPU%util dropped 72% -> 53%. See /bench/185123/prof.log

Marta Diaz: My guess is head packing + page fragmentation. If num_kv_heads isn't divisible by the kernel warp packing factor, selector picks a fallback. Try 32 or 128 heads or pad head slots. Also paged layout can fragment hot slots across pages which increases memcpy / kernel launches.

Jorge Alvarez: Also check batching heuristics. We saw the runtime shrinking batch windows when prefix cache hits vary widely across requests. Continuous batching default max_tokens might be too low for this workload, causing more small kernels. Try increasing continuous_batching.max_tokens to 4096 and continuous_batching.max_clients to 8.

Priya Rao: Could be RoPE scaling influencing kernel choice too — some optimized kernels assume standard rotary params for fused kernels. If rope_scale != 1.0 the kernel selector currently penalizes optimized path. That logic might be overly conservative.

Alex Chen: Re-ran quick experiments: padded num_key_value_heads to 128 (zero-pad slots) -> throughput up ~18% (400 tok/s) and GPU util to 78%, but p95 still high and CPU memcpy increased. So padding helps kernel selection, but paged KV fragmentation still causes tail stalls when hot keys spread across pages.

Marta Diaz: We should add a head-slotting allocator: when paged and GQA, place hot heads contiguously so a fused kernel can operate on them with fewer pages. Also expose a kv_page_compaction flag to compact hot slots periodically.

perf-bot: quick profile snippet (hot spans):
```
ATTN_FUSED_KERNEL: launches 12 -> 120ms total
ATTN_GENERIC_KERNEL: launches 84 -> 680ms total
KV_PAGE_COPY: 312 ops -> 54ms total (CPU memcpy dominates)
GPU_UTIL: 53% -> 78% after padding
```

Jorge Alvarez: Another lever — batching heuristic: prefer coalescing requests that hit same cache page (prefix coalescing). If we detect identical page IDs in request set, coalesce into single KV read and apply to N in-flight queries. That reduces memcpy and kernel launches.

Priya Rao: Steps I recommend: 
1) Add a kernel-hint flag to force fused kernel when heads % warp==0 or when padded.
2) Implement head-slotting heuristic in paged allocator.
3) Add kv_page_compaction and tune page_size (64/128/256) in microbench.
4) Relax the rope_scale penalty in kernel selector, re-run selection tests.
5) Add a microbenchmark CI job for mixtral/qwen/llama with varying heads & rope_scale.

Alex Chen: I'll run A/B overnight. Command I'm using: 
```
./tools/bench --model mixtral-8x7b --kv-layout paged --heads 64,128 --page-size 64,128,256 --rope-scale 1.0,1.8 --batch-max-tokens 4096 --repeat 12 --output /tmp/185123
```
Posting results in the morning. Tagging @Infra SRE to spin up CI job for cross-model runs (mixtral/qwen/llama2).

Infra SRE: Got it — I'll schedule an overnight matrix, include pinned GPU types and ensure perf counters are collected. Will also add a small perfwatch alert if p50 or throughput regresses >15%.

Marta Diaz: Also add a quick instrumentation probe: per-page hotness map + fragmentation ratio (free_pages / used_pages) and head-contiguity score. We can feed that into selector to prefer contiguous packing.

Alex Chen: Thanks — I'll attach traces and a couple flamegraphs when done. If we can get fused kernel back on for the common head configs, we should recover most of the lost throughput.

Priya Rao: SGTM. If this turns into a kernel bug (wrong assumptions on RoPE params), we may need a short patch to the optimized kernels. Keep us posted. :thumbsup:

Alex Chen: Will do. Closing for tonight, will post new thread with bench results tomorrow.
